data.description:
Spine task 2 of D1 v1. Create apps/invoicing/ — the product application — in the stack chosen by the stack-decision task: docker compose service(s), configuration loading, a test harness, and a health endpoint. The acceptance property that matters: docker compose up starts the app and the full test suite passes with NO external services, NO accounts, and NO network egress. Everything after this depends on that property continuing to hold.

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 row C-02 (IN — Rule 1: nothing in the chain runs without it). Section 8.3 spine task 2.

DECISION CONTEXT. The directory name apps/invoicing/ is decided, not a placeholder. Under the company-name record docs/strategy/09-company-name.md section 8.2, the monorepo/internal-infra layer carries generic descriptive names and the product brand attaches at the extraction seam and on customer-facing surfaces (deploy domains, sender domains, app chrome). The product has no name yet and this directory never needs to change when it gets one — which is also why naming does not block the scaffold. Follow apps/chat/ for compose and test-runner conventions unless the stack decision chose otherwise; note that the chat app is internal tooling and its zero-dependency convention is evidence, not a mandate, for the product.

VERIFICATION: docker compose up serves the health endpoint; the test suite runs green from a clean checkout with the network unavailable. Both are runnable today with no accounts.

NOT IN THIS TASK: the data model or any table (the data-model task); any Stripe code whatsoever — the custody guard lands before any Stripe caller and this task must not front-run it with a "temporary" client; authentication; any UI screen (screens are wireframe-gated on AS-30).
data.title: D1 v1: apps/invoicing scaffold — compose stack, config, test harness, health check

data.note: spine: scaffold cannot start before the stack is chosen

data.body:
PLAN FILED. Branch feat/AS-37-invoicing-scaffold, worktree .worktrees/AS-37. Marcus implements from the plan file alone; everything binding is quoted or cited there.

THE TWO GAPS AS-36's REVIEW LEFT ME, both closed by measurement rather than assertion.

(1) PINS. The decision mandates exact pins and never names them. Named now, measured 2026-09-01: express@5.2.1 (MIT), ejs@6.0.1 (Apache-2.0), base image node:24.20.0-slim (exact patch, stronger than the mandated exact minor). Plus the rule that regenerates them if npm has moved: pin the latest stable at implementation time as an exact literal, re-walk the tree, and STOP for a board ask if any licence is non-permissive or the direct set is anything but {express, ejs}.

ADOPTED TRANSITIVE FOOTPRINT, stated for the first time (QA finding 3): 2 direct, 67 distinct name@version, 69 instances, 4.0 MB, image 239 MB (+9 MB over base). Licence spread 61 MIT / 4 ISC / 1 Apache-2.0 / 1 BSD-3-Clause, zero non-permissive. Flagged in the plan: 67 is coincidentally the same number the decision reports for C2-WITH-Zod. It is arithmetic (Zod out, version drift in), not transcription — instances moved 70->69 and disk 12 MB->4.0 MB, consistent with 10.3.

A TRAP the decision does not warn about: 'npm install express@5.2.1' writes '^5.2.1' — a caret range, which section 12 explicitly forbids. Measured. Fix is --save-exact plus a committed lockfile plus npm ci only, and section 9.6 of the plan makes it a test rather than a review convention.

(2) TOKENS.CSS. Mechanism: repo-root build context (context ../.., dockerfile apps/invoicing/Dockerfile) with COPY docs/design/tokens/tokens.css ./vendor/tokens.css, served by an explicit named route registered before express.static. 'No copy' read as: exactly one copy in version control, and what is served is byte-identical to it — the only reading consistent with section 12's own Content-Length verification.

SPIKED, NOT REASONED. Built under BuildKit AND the legacy builder (chat's compose documents that this host sometimes exports DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0, which is why additional_contexts was rejected — BuildKit-only). Suite exit 0 under --network none. Served: 200, Content-Length 12199, body 12,199 bytes, byte-identical to the image source. MUTATION: delete the COPY line, rebuild — suite exits 1. The guard is not vacuous. Bind mount rejected because it puts the file out of reach of the mountless test service, so byte-identity could only ever be asserted lexically, never fetched.

VACUITY FLOOR (eight prior vacuous passes: AS-17, AS-26, four in AS-29 cycle 1, one in AS-29 hardening, one in AS-31's checker). Three structural properties from day one. V1: harness.test.js fails under ASC_SELFTEST_MUTATE=1, so one command in both directions proves the test service runs the suite, a failure produces a non-zero exit, and compose surfaces it — a runner never observed to go red is not evidence, same argument the decision made for validating --network none with both controls. V2: cardinality before quantification — every assertion quantified over a discovered set is preceded by an exact-count assertion against a committed literal (183 token declarations, the suite's own file count, the direct dependency set). V3: the container is the subject — deployed-shape properties are asserted from inside the mountless test service against the real image.

HEALTH CHECK. Design rule: a health check may only assert things that can be FALSE while the process is still able to answer. Three checks as data (config, vendor_assets, views), 200 only if all pass, 503 with the failing check named. Each must be demonstrated able to fail or it is decoration. Stripe and the DB are deliberately absent — AS-39 appends a row, which is why the checks are a list.

PORT 8348. Measured free; 8347 is asc-chat-server-1 and is not to be disturbed; 3001/4000/4100/5432/7700/8799 are held by unrelated containers.

DIVERGENCES FROM apps/chat, argued not inherited: routes/ + a thin composition root (the decision's load-bearing finding is that hand-rolled code leaves module boundaries to discipline, and this company has two measured observations of that discipline not holding); express.static + an enumeration test instead of chat's STATIC_FILES allowlist (AS-17 was a missing allowlist entry — express.static has no second edit to forget, and the enumeration test closes its own failure direction); config injected into app.js so no test mutates process.env. Mirrored: compose-only, mountless test service, bare node --test, bind 0.0.0.0 inside with loopback on the host side, manifests COPY'd as data for a deploy-shape test.

PLATFORM PIN: kept at linux/amd64. My prior was that emulation would tax every suite run since we install 67 packages where chat installs none. Measured 3x3: native 1.63/1.59/1.56 s, emulated 1.58/1.47/1.49 s — no measurable tax, the suite is startup-dominated. Prior falsified, pin stands.

ONE HARNESS RULE that cost me a probe: register teardown BEFORE the assertions (t.after), never after. A probe that closed its listener on the line after a failing assert HUNG with no output until killed. A hung suite is worse than a red one — no exit code, no output.

MUST NOT FORECLOSE (AS-38's guard is not this task's job, but a scaffold can quietly make it unenforceable): no outbound HTTP client anywhere outside test/ — the decision chose the hand-rolled client precisely because the only bypass is a second HTTP client and fetch/node:http call sites are greppable; no stripe dep, no STRIPE_* key, no /webhook, no application_fee; no money type (AS-39 owns integer minor units + currency); network_mode: none is not negotiable (T3); dependency budget stays at 2, enforced by a test.

NO ACCOUNT ASSUMED. AS-51 is open and stays off the critical path: no setting is required, no credential is named, no .env of any kind, and the acceptance property is that the suite passes with a COMPLETELY EMPTY environment. The optional-secret mechanism and redaction are built and tested now against a fixture schema, so AS-38 inherits a tested mechanism rather than an untested one.

WRITE-BACKS OWED to docs/engineering/01-stack-decision.md section 13, to be filed as a backlog task (not AS-37's — it must not amend the decision it implements): the pins and adopted footprint; T4 gains an upgrade clause re-running the transitive licence scan (QA finding 2, ACCEPTED — nothing today re-scans the 67 admitted packages when Express or EJS is upgraded, and section 5.3 is the proof that a tree is where a licence problem hides); and the caret-range trap.

ZERO SPEND. Two MIT/Apache-2.0 packages, no account, no service, no purchase.
